labels.text: ### [Self Guided Walking Tour San Telmo](…)
I'm the type of person that do Excel sheet for each travel itinerary and like to plan ahead everything.
That's how I come across for the first time to a Self-Guided Walking Tour post in Edinburgh, and I was like, wow this is amazing.
After living 8 years in San Telmo, Buenos Aires I kind of feel ready to do a Guide myself.
So here is a 24hs tour to the Center, San Telmo, La Boca and Defensa.
Be ready to walk around 15km and eat delicious food in the way :) I hope you enjoy it!
\* Note: this tour was though to be done not on Sunday.
Since San Telmo has a HUGE street fair during Sundays and is a bit crowded, but it can be done anyway maybe we a bit more time.
\* *There is a map at the end with all the stops mentioned!*
**9am - Teatro Colón**  The itinerary starts from the   Subte station "Tribunales".
labels.reason: Announces starting the tour at a metro station.

labels.text: From there you can cross the park   to see the stunning Teatro Colón from outside.
labels.reason: Directs traveller to see Teatro Colón.

labels.text: Then you can walk a few streets to  see the Obelisco and then walkthrough  Av. Roque Saenz Peña directly  to Plaza de Mayo.
labels.reason: Directs to Plaza de Mayo via avenue and obelisk.

labels.text: **10am - Have Breakfast and visit Plaza de Mayo**
Picture by[@andregrevex](…)
Once you arrive to Plaza de Mayo you can walk through Av. de Mayo (which is really beautiful avenue) at the end of this avenue you can see the Congress building.
labels.reason: Directs walking through avenue towards Congress.

labels.text: Here I recommend you 2 coffees shop:  **-** the first is the iconic **Café** **Tortoni**, you can enjoy some "Cafe con medialunas" this is our typical breakfast.
However Tortoni has also nice "Churros con Chocolate".
**-**In case Tortoni is too crowded you can walk back to **London City Coffee** where multiple famous writers and iconic figures of Buenos Aires spent time there, such as our writer Cortázar.
Counter of Tortoni Café, Buenos Aires
Then you can walk back through Av. de Mayo and reach Plaza de Mayo again.
labels.reason: Directs back to Plaza de Mayo.

labels.text: This Plaza is quite important here we have the Casa Rosada, the Cathedral (where the Pope use to give mass) and the Cabildo.
Is a place where most of the manifestation take place since is connected to Congress.

[TEXTALT](…)        You can see in the floor of Plaza de Mayo some white Scarfs draw in the floor, this represents the "Grandmother of Plaza de Mayo", this are grandmothers you ask until today for their missing grandchildren during the dictatorship.
labels.reason: Points out details in the plaza.

labels.text: \*\* If you want to enter Casa Rosada, you have to book a visit in advance, they are free.
labels.reason: Provides tips and booking info for Casa Rosada.

labels.text: Stunning picture by [@aguspiluso](…)
**12 am - Walk through Defensa Street**  Now you are entering San Telmo.
labels.reason: Walking Defensa Street is presented as an itinerary stop.

labels.text: Defensa Street is the main street and on Sunday there is a huge street fair that starts from Plaza de Mayo and continues to Plaza Dorrego.
labels.reason: Mentions locations for orientation and context.

labels.text: -  Stop 5: is a really old Pharmacy call **"Farmacia la Estrella"**, from 1834.
labels.reason: Stop 5 directs the traveller to visit Farmacia la Estrella.

labels.text: Take a look inside and to its beautiful sealing!.
labels.reason: Directs the traveller to look inside the pharmacy.

labels.text: Just in from is a small Museum of the city, sometimes they have exhibitions about local products or traditions, is free to enter so feel free to give it a look.

entities.sourceName: a small Museum of the city
entities.supportSpan: a small Museum of the city

labels.reason: Directs the traveller to enter the city museum.

labels.text: - Stop 6: Oldest library in town, **"La Librería del Avila"**!, this is the library it has more than 100.000 books and it has been witness of big part of our history.
labels.reason: Stop 6 directs the traveller to visit La Librería del Avila.

labels.text: Is used to be call the "School Library" because if you look just in front, you can see the prestigious National School of Buenos Aires.
labels.reason: Mentions the school seen in front.

labels.text: 🥩 If you are hungry at this point and want to have launch, I highly recommend having lunch at [Alfonso](…) (in Av. Belgrano 782) cozy place with comfort food and very nice selection of wines and vermouth.
labels.reason: Recommends a specific restaurant for lunch.

labels.text: - Stop 7: **Monumento de Mafalda**, this is one of our most loved cartoon characters created by Quino.
labels.reason: Stop 7 directs the traveller to visit the monument.

labels.text: If you never heard of it, it was translated in almost any language and although it looks like a cartoon for kids it talks about world issues about politics and economics that is almost as relevant for adults.
Mafalda use to live in San Telmo exactly in a house in Chile 371 that actually exists, so you can check it out!
labels.reason: Suggests checking out Mafalda's former house.

labels.text: Casa Mínima, San Telmo, Buenos Aires
- Stop 8: **Casa Mínima**, this is known to be the narrowest house in Buenos Aires, not sure if this is true but is cute and the street as well ;)
labels.reason: Stop 8 directs the traveller to Casa Mínima.

labels.text: 4 días en Mendoza, Argentina - Itinerario completo día por día de que hacer.
labels.reason: Irrelevant Mendoza itinerary ad or header.

labels.text: Stop 9: **The San Telmo Market**!!
labels.reason: Stop 9 directs the traveller to the market.

labels.text: My favorite place in the neighborhood, the oldest market in Buenos Aires and recently  remodeled with a lot of restaurants  (before there were antiquities  and fruit and and vegetable stores).
Here there are also a lot of  tourist traps, so be careful.
labels.reason: Provides a warning about tourist traps.

labels.text: Here you have 2 choices, have lunch in the market, or grab something  small and wait to eat some  big meal in La Boca.
labels.reason: Offers a choice of where to eat lunch.

labels.text: 🌭If you go for the small bite, I recommend eating *1 choripan* en **Nuestra Parrilla** (stop 10), is on the outside (over Bolivar street) of the market and not a tourist trap.
labels.reason: Recommends a specific food spot as an alternative choice.

labels.text: 🍦Exactly on the opposite side, also on the outside side, in Defensa street you have 2 icecream shops ( if you didn't notice we love ice cream here and we eat a lot of it!)
labels.reason: Mentions generic ice cream shops without specific names.

labels.text: ☕️If you are craving for some coffee, go to **Coffee Town**, just in the middle of the market, is the best in area!
labels.reason: Recommends Coffee Town for coffee as an option.

labels.text: 🥩 If you for the BIG meal, my favorite restaurant is **Saigón** is kind of Vietnamese - Argentine, I highly recommend trying the Bo Lu Lac (Is meat with rice).
labels.reason: Recommends Saigón for a big meal.

labels.text: But I understand if you want to eat asado, so here I would recommend to go to **Desnivel**, is not fancy but you eat really good!
labels.reason: Recommends Desnivel as an alternative restaurant.

labels.text: Café Rivas, San Telmo, Bueos Aires
**Café Rivas y Galería Solar**    This are two other places you can  visit while you are around.
labels.reason: Presents two optional places to visit.

labels.text: The first  one is Café Rivas, a beautiful café.
labels.reason: Describes one of the optional places.

labels.text: Just one block from the San Telmo Market you can find the Galería Solar, this use  to be an old house that is now full of shops.
- Stop 10: Last stop, this is "**El Patio de los Ezeiza"**.
labels.reason: Presents stop 10 as an itinerary destination.

labels.text: This is a house that was built around 1876 to house the Ezeiza family, an aristocratic family.
labels.reason: Provides historical information about the house.

labels.text: Later, the Ezeiza would leave the house to move to Barrio Norte, like many other upper class families in Buenos Aires during the Yellow Fever Epidemic of 1871.
After this is become a school, later a *conventillo* and right now is full of shop so you can just wonder around!
Patio Ezeiza, San Telmo, Buenos Aires, Argentina
**15hs - Go to Caminito en La Boca**
From "El Patio de los Ezeiza" you can take bus 29 to Caminito or take a taxi.
The taxi should cost about 3usd max (official USD, not the blue USD). You can use Google Maps to get here, it works pretty ok with the buses.
labels.reason: Provides practical tips and cost details for the transfer.

labels.text: **CAMINITO, LA BOCA**  An important note here, La Boca is the  neighborhood and is not the type   of neighborhood you want to be at night.
labels.reason: Heading and safety warning about the neighborhood.

labels.text: However, Caminito is the tourist street   of this neighborhood.
labels.reason: Describes Caminito as the tourist street.

labels.text: My advice  here is: first, if it is getting darker   rather leave this for another day,  if you choose to go to Caminito, wonder  only where you see tourists, don't go  go beyond this, because as I said,  is not the most friendly  neighborhood out there.
The tourist part you will notice  is the one with colorful houses  and is about 3-4 blocks.
You might be hungry by this point, so:   - 🥩 Stop 13: **"Don Carlos"** also recommended by Anthony Bourdain in his episode of Parts Unknown in Buenos Aires.
A small restaurant run by a family in front of the "Estadio La Boca".
labels.reason: Describes the restaurant and Estadio La Boca.

labels.text: You sit here and the owner will bring you food, no question ask, until you cant not walk anymore and decide to stop eating what it will become one of your best food memories.
-  Stop 12: After this, you can wander around **Caminito Street**, and maybe check the "**Fundación Proa**" sometimes they have interesting exhibitions.
labels.reason: Directs to Caminito Street and optional Fundación Proa.

labels.text: **17 / 18hs - Go to Puerto Madero**  Here as well you can take a bus or a taxi for around 3,8usd.
The starting point here is the **Puente de la Mujer**, this is beautiful day or night.
By crossing this bridge you are officially in Puerto Madero, and no wonder that you will see that all streets have suddenly women names.
labels.reason: Mentions entering Puerto Madero by crossing the bridge.

labels.text: Here is there is not much to do more than walking and seeing the contrast of such a new architecture just in from of the oldest neighborhood such as San Telmo.
labels.reason: Mentions San Telmo as a contrast seen from the walk.

labels.text: I like to walk next to the "Darsena Sur" and then through Av. Int. Hernan Giralt that is close to an ecological park.
If you are hungry at this point I can recommend:  - 🌭 Salad: eat *a choripan* in some of the kiosk over  Av. Int. Hernan Giralt.
**20hs - Return home / hotel**    If you return through the marked path, you can see the "Centro Cultural Kirchner" that used to be our old Central Post Office.
They offer guided tours and maybe you can enter to see a part of the building.
From here you will see the Metrobus with the main buses or it is quite a busy street so you can take a taxi!
labels.reason: Mentions taking a taxi or metrobus.

labels.text: 🍹 Stop 16: Or if you feel like continuing and having a little celebration drink, I highly recommend one of our few sky bars in town: [Trade Sky Bar](…).
Is better to book in advance!
It has an amazing view of Puerto madero.
labels.reason: Describes the view from a previous stop.

labels.text: I also recommend this [36hs in Buenos Aires New York Times Guide](…).
Totally love it an agree in all the places and you can have a taste of the other neighborhoods in Buenos Aires :)    I really hope you liked this self-guided tour in San Telmo!
labels.reason: Concluding author remarks and final thoughts.
